focus: Angle 2: providers, models and the subscription
noveltyJustification: All eight findings are new: the two credential families, the declarative provider and model rows, the fetched model catalogue, reasoning as a model field rather than a flag, the Vibe Code budget counter, the plan-label mapping and the local cost record had no prior capture.
keyQuestions: How does Vibe run one task non-interactively: which prompt source, flags, output formats and exit codes does the headless contract expose?
Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?

label: Two credential families: a first-party mistral provider with browser sign-in (OIDC via console.mistral.ai) or MISTRAL_API_KEY, and BYOK providers with their own api_base and api_key_env_var; third-party credentials never reach first-party endpoints.
Providers are declarative openai-style rows (api_base, api_key_env_var, api_style, backend, vertex project/region, extra_headers); only mistral and a local llamacpp endpoint ship by default.

Models are declarative rows (name, provider, alias, temperature, thinking levels, prices, context length); pinning deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017 or zai-glm-5-3-flash is a provider row plus a model row each, and no roster ships beyond one default model.
The Mistral model catalogue is fetched from <api_base>/model-catalog?surface=vibe-code with a 5s cap and 30-day TTL; BYOK providers rely only on declared rows.
Reasoning effort has no dispatch flag: it is the per-model thinking field plus thinking_levels, so a governed executor pins it in the model row or agent profile.

A Vibe turn draws on the org's monthly Vibe Code allowance, read from /v1/billing/budget with plan and pay-as-you-go from /v1/billing/subscription; both are optional and read as None when unavailable.
Plan labels come from /whoami: chat Free/Pro/Student/Team, Mistral Code Free Codestral/Code Enterprise, API Free API/PAYG API; the label is display data, the budget read is the counter.
Per-dispatch cost is locally computable: export.json carries usage, cost_usd, steps and subagent costs, priced from the model row's per-million rates.
